teams.heading: Fiji Rugby confirm interest in recruiting Mark Nawaqanitawase for 2027 World Cup
teams.body: Fiji Rugby have confirmed interest in recruiting Mark Nawaqanitawase for the 2027 World Cup in Australia. Les Kiss has also weighed in on the prospect. The move would land as Jake White takes charge of a side ranked 10th in the world that has lost four of five Tests this year. Fiji are in Pool C at the World Cup alongside Argentina, Canada and Spain.

lead.why: A men's squad story with a sharper angle than the earlier 'interest' coverage, though the shortlist lists it as background, first seen 5 days ago.

teams.heading: Feyi-Waboso leads Prem defenders-beaten chart with 24 as Australia Test nears
teams.body: The club Prem's stats leaders have England's Immanuel Feyi-Waboso at the top of the defenders-beaten table, with 24 after three rounds of the 2026/27 season. That is five more than Sale's Joe Carpenter and eight clear of Bristol's Louis Rees-Zammit on 16. Exeter's winger has also made 265 metres from three games, a sign of how much the power game runs through him as Borthwick's Australia Test approaches.

lead.why: It is a fresh Prem stats item that puts England's Feyi-Waboso at the top of a key attacking metric, and the story that led the 19-20 October editions has already run.

teams.heading: Clermont Auvergne club: protests turn to clashes with police as Leinster win
teams.body: Clermont Auvergne's weekend was overshadowed by unrest in the city: protests on Saturday turned into clashes between demonstrators and police while Leinster were winning at the Stade Marcel-Michelin. The supporters The42 met across the weekend are intensely passionate but worried about the club's future, and one admits he would accept relegation to ProD2 if it brought change at the top.

teams.heading: Munster's Brian Gleeson pushes for Ireland call as Jack Conan faces assessment
teams.body: Munster are hopeful Brian Gleeson will be included in Andy Farrell's Ireland squad, which is due to be named on Wednesday. The 22-year-old number eight has been in Farrell's camp before, and the doubts over Jack Conan's shoulder, which needs further assessment, plus Caelan Doris's absence through injury, open a door. Gleeson has started the season strongly, with a powerful showing in Munster's win over Racing 92 on Saturday. Connacht's Sean Jansen remains a rival for the spot.

lead.why: A new national-squad selection angle on Brian Gleeson, with Conan's injury doubt and Doris's absence opening a possible door for him.

teams.heading: Italy, winners once in their last five, next face South Africa
teams.body: Italy have won one of their last five, and the next task is South Africa in Round 4 of the Nations Championship. The current run is four straight defeats; the latest came away to Australia in July, who won 57-10. Across their three matches, Italy have no wins and have conceded 131 points while scoring 37.

teams.heading: Scotland's former captain Stuart Hogg loses MBE after domestic abuse conviction
teams.body: Stuart Hogg's MBE was removed in March after his domestic abuse conviction, and the Cabinet Office's official register lists him among 15 people stripped of honours in 2026. Hogg won 100 caps for Scotland, toured three times with the British and Irish Lions and was twice named Six Nations Player of the Championship. He pleaded guilty to a domestic abuse charge involving his estranged wife and received a one-year community payback order in January 2025.

lead.why: It is the strongest genuinely new item in the shortlist, and it concerns a former Scotland captain rather than the Glasgow debut already run today.

teams.heading: Tomos Williams has started every Test he's been available for under Tandy
teams.body: Tomos Williams is the first name on Wales's scrum-half list, and that is becoming a planning question. He has started every Test he has been available for since Steve Tandy took over in the summer of 2025, and played 378 minutes of the 2026 Six Nations. Behind him, Kieran Hardy faces a lengthy lay-off after a knee injury against Dragons, which could open the door for Reuben Morgan-Williams. Tandy names his squad today.

teams.heading: Shaun Edwards joins Argentina as defence coach after England stint
teams.body: Shaun Edwards has joined Argentina as defence coach, a move that rules him out of a role in Steve Borthwick's England set-up, according to reports carried since 10 October. Coverage frames it as Argentina landing a high-profile defensive specialist from England, and one headline says the appointment will bolster Argentina's World Cup bid. Coverage has not yet reported his first Test series under the system, so the storyline stays open until Los Pumas play it with him in charge.

lead.why: It is the only item in today's pack that concerns Argentina's own coaching staff, and it is a concrete appointment rather than commentary.

teams.heading: Harry Wilson says Wallabies can't keep having terrible halves against All Blacks
teams.body: Captain Harry Wilson wants a sharper start after Saturday's second Bledisloe Test, a 43-21 loss in Sydney that was the Wallabies' 13th straight defeat to New Zealand. Australia trailed 36-7 at half-time. "We can’t be having terrible halves against the All Blacks," Wilson told Channel Nine, while Les Kiss called the first-half showing unacceptable and the Wallabies face next year's World Cup with plenty to fix.

lead.why: It carries on-record reaction from captain Harry Wilson and coach Les Kiss to Saturday's loss, a different angle from the Suaalii and McKenzie items already run.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones suspended four games, salary cut, over abuse of officials
teams.body: Japan's federation has suspended Eddie Jones for four games and cut his salary over "verbal abuse directed at local officials" during the Under-23 tour of Australia in April. The ban rules him out of the Nations Championship opener against Italy and the Japan XV game against the Maori All Blacks. Jones has accepted the sanction, saying: "I deeply regret my behaviour and words." The Japan Rugby Football Union announced the penalty in May.

teams.heading: Hansen praises All Blacks' running lines and handling in Bledisloe win
teams.body: Sir Steve Hansen believes the All Blacks are finally being rewarded for Dave Rennie's attacking work, calling their running lines "sublime" in Saturday's 43-21 win over Australia in Sydney. Speaking on the Rugby Unity podcast, he singled out big forwards taking short and long balls into space, Codie Taylor's handling under pressure and Cam Roigard's willingness to pass in the tackle. The win sealed a 2-0 Bledisloe series after the 50-19 win at Eden Park.

lead.why: It is the freshest men's All Blacks item on the shortlist, and it is about the side's own attacking play rather than the injury list already covered.

teams.heading: Wales follow Rassie Erasmus' lead, hiring referee Ben Whitehouse as full-time coach
teams.body: Wales have taken a page from Rassie Erasmus' playbook, with the WRU naming referee Ben Whitehouse a full-time specialist coach for the men's squad to work on law, discipline, decision-making and communication. It mirrors the role Jaco Peyper has filled with the Springboks since 2024, when he joined the Springbok management as national laws advisor. Whitehouse, 36, is set to hang up his whistle after Saturday's URC clash between the Ospreys and Dragons.

lead.why: It is a fresh, concrete appointment that borrows directly from the Springbok model, and Tony Brown's quote has already run today.
